title: ChessFlyStatePings: state-bearing history meets a frozen connectome chess network
summary: Takes BrainAsInverseModelerV3's narrow state-bearing-event / receiver-readout idea into a real pretrained artificial network built on ChessFly's connectome-derived recurrent graph. The first recurrent StatePing intervention mostly collapsed to a gain change because fast-minus-slow residue was almost collinear with present activity and did not establish stronger play. The follow-up orthogonal-history gate explicitly removed the present-state direction and compared the remaining temporal direction with shuffled, re-orthogonalized, norm-matched controls. In the post-fix CUDA smoke run, only about 3.03% of residue norm survived orthogonalization, yet the real temporal direction ranked around the 94.4th percentile for value-logit sensitivity and 86.4th percentile at the shared association layer, while policy-logit sensitivity was much less unusual at about the 68.2nd percentile. This is preliminary receiver-dependent readability evidence, not a chess-strength or biological-code result.

nodes.claim: Tests whether a tiny history-dependent direction, separated from present activation, is read differently by frozen downstream heads in ChessFly's connectome-derived recurrent chess network.
nodes.survived: The naive recurrent StatePing perturbation was stable but mostly acted like gain because fast-minus-slow residue was nearly parallel to current activity. After projecting that present-state component away, the post-fix CUDA Gate 1b run used 3 positions and 32 shuffled, re-orthogonalized, norm-matched controls per position with zero instabilities. Only about 3.03% of residue norm survived (about 0.0929% squared energy), yet the real history direction reached mean value-logit percentiles of 94.4%, 94.4%, and 93.4% at magnitudes 1, 2, and 4, with 86.4% association-layer percentile and 68.2% policy-logit percentile. At magnitude 2, value-logit RMS sensitivity was about 1.88x the matched-control mean, association change about 1.32x, and policy-logit RMS about 1.12x. A float32 Jensen-Shannon underflow found by the first run was fixed with float64 log-space evaluation and the rerun remained finite.
nodes.killed: The first StatePing mechanism did not establish stronger chess and should not be described as adding new information; in this five-step regime its residue mostly duplicated the current-state direction. The orthogonal-history result is still only a three-position smoke test, does not show improved playing strength, and does not establish a biological spike-waveform or synaptic-readout mechanism.
nodes.era: Receiver-dependent history readout in a pretrained connectome network

edges.why: ChessFlyStatePings explicitly takes V3's narrow distinction between state present at an event and state readable by a downstream receiver, then tests that distinction in a frozen pretrained artificial network with separate association, policy, and value readouts.
